evidence.paraphrase: The skipper describes reverting his ship from petrol motors back to sail after the engines proved too costly.
evidence.quote:
I tried to get rich by puttin’ in they petrol motors, and hangin’ screw astarn. I thought they
newfangled boats were the thing; but--it cost so much to run ’em
they didn’t pay. So us has sold they engines, and had ’em hauled
out, and--the _I’ll Try_ be just the same as she was when I built
her, livin’ by her sails and the winds of the Lord Almighty.

evidence.paraphrase: The narration contrasts the outdated hand-winch of the I'll Try with more modern equipment used elsewhere.
evidence.quote: The _I\u2019ll Try_ be one of the last ships\nleft that has to hoist trawls by hand-winch and--great dollops, it\ndo be hard work!

evidence.paraphrase: The winch mechanism fails violently during the storm, releasing the load and spinning the bars.
evidence.quote:
The winch-dogs, which worked against cogs, snapped
with the vicious sharpness of a high explosive. The whole weight of
the warp, the surging ship and the storm was instantly released. The
long bars of the winch spun like a huge, malevolent top.

evidence.paraphrase: The captain reacts to being injured and disoriented after the winch accident.
evidence.quote: Captain Josh, stunned, dazed, confused, lifted himself from the heap\ninto which he had been thrown against the weather bulwarks, wondered\nwhy a red blanket blurred his vision

evidence.paraphrase: The narration explains how the trawl gear operates and how it snagged on a suspected wreck.
evidence.quote:
The great net, held open by a forty-foot
beam and towed along the bottom of the sea floor upon “trawl-heads”
that were like huge steel sled-runners, had caught what the men of
the _I’ll Try_ surmised must be a sunken wreck.

evidence.paraphrase: The captain reasons out his position and course by dead reckoning from known factors.
evidence.quote:
He made mental calculations, reasoning that in the
beginning the _I’ll Try_ must have been so many miles sou’west off
the reef-bordered Prawl Point, that the wind had come from due west,
and that therefore it must be safe to run.

evidence.paraphrase: The rescuing crew reacts with awe and bewilderment at the old captain's singing.
evidence.quote:
The voice that came quavering across the sullen waves, as if
blanketed by the leaden skies, held the men of the _Williwaw_ in its
spell. They clung to the rail, staring with perplexed eyes and
parted lips

evidence.paraphrase: The narration juxtaposes the tiny earnings from the catch against the high costs of burial, contradicting the opening letter's claims.
evidence.quote:
the catch of the _I’ll Try_
brought six pounds, fourteen shillings and sixpence--nearly
twenty-six dollars, to be divided amongst the sole survivors of the
hapless crew. Captain Joshua’s share as owner and skipper came to
nearly four pounds, or sixteen dollars! The undertaker charged
fifteen pounds--about sixty dollars--for the coffin
